## Overview
Computes SART sensitivity (d′) for each participant using signal detection theory. Hits are correct responses on go trials and false alarms are commission errors on no-go trials. A log-linear correction keeps hit and false-alarm rates of 0 or 1 from producing infinite values. Outputs one d′ score per participant.

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
library(dplyr)

data <- read.csv("~/Desktop/research/Elton/SARA/sara_data_VM.csv")

data <- data %>%
  mutate(
    hits = 200 - err_om,
    misses = err_om,
    false_alarms = err_com,
    correct_rejections = 25 - err_com,

    hit_rate = (hits + 0.5) / 201,
    fa_rate = (false_alarms + 0.5) / 26,

    d_prime = qnorm(hit_rate) - qnorm(fa_rate)
  )
print(data$d_prime)

out <- data[, c("filename1", "d_prime")]
write.csv(out, "~/Desktop/sart_dprime.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```
